clue.text: Suitable wear for a Digger?

parts.note: a Digger is an Australian soldier, and soldiers in the Great War dug and lived in trenches, so the garment is named after where they served

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digger' is Australian and New Zealand slang for a soldier; the capital D hides that sense behind someone with a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: This belted waterproof was designed for officers serving in the dug-out lines of the Western Front.

clue.text: First into the Weird Sisters' pot

definitions.text: First into the Weird Sisters' pot

parts.words: First into the Weird Sisters' pot
parts.note: in Macbeth the three witches name the ingredients of their charmed cauldron, and the first thrown in is a creature that sleeps under cold stone

explanation.walkthrough: The Weird Sisters are the three witches in Shakespeare's Macbeth; their spell begins 'Round about the cauldron go'.
explanation.definitionFit: The witches' recipe opens with this warty amphibian, the first creature dropped into their cauldron.

clue.text: Artemus is unskilled in running birds

indicators.note: unskilled means lacking skill, so the name Artemus loses the letters spelling a word for skill

explanation.surface: A man named Artemus has no talent for racing birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Art is skill, so 'Artemus is unskilled' takes ART off the name.
explanation.definitionFit: These large Australian birds cannot fly but run fast across open country.

clue.text: A bugle call is the nicest part of exercises!

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters within the words before it

explanation.surface: The bugle signal is the best bit of military drill.
explanation.definitionFit: These are gymnastic exercises for strength and grace, done without equipment.

clue.text: Commanding Officer looks down on honour that is hollow.

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits above, looking down on, the second

parts.note: the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A senior officer sneers at a decoration that means nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' looks like an adjective (empty honour) but is the noun: a small valley, chiefly in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short valley or deep hollow in a hillside.

clue.text: Poses in a sober-suited fashion

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape or reshape, so the letters of suited are made over

explanation.surface: Models strike stances in a manner fitting a soberly dressed person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' here rearranges SUITED into ITUDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are bodily postures, as a dancer or model strikes them.

clue.text: Kill off with this blow

explanation.surface: An assassin chooses the single stroke that will finish off a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition fills a gap: 'kill off with this' word, as in the gangland phrase for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump someone off is slang for murdering them, and a bump is also a knock or thump.

clue.text: Crypt's crude front. needs rebuilding

indicators.note: rebuilding means the letters of the two words are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The rough frontage of a church crypt has to be reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Crypt' with the 's read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An undercroft is a vaulted underground chamber beneath a church, the same as a crypt.

clue.text: Be responsible for itemizing each lamb, say, by value

parts.note: per means for each item, as in so much per head
a lamb is an example of a pet, a tame animal
rate as a noun means value or price

explanation.surface: Someone is in charge of listing the worth of every lamb in a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate is to commit, carry out a crime or blunder.

clue.text: Bright name for a caveman

parts.note: the Victorian MP John Bright mocked rebel Liberals by naming them after the followers who gathered round David in the cave of Adullam

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' looks like 'clever' but is John Bright, the Victorian radical politician who coined the nickname in 1866.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, discontented men joined David in the cave of Adullam, so a dweller there is a caveman.

clue.text: Scent, say, of border flower?

indicators.note: say tells us the word for scent is spoken, and the entry is something sounding like it

parts.note: a scent is a smell or odour

explanation.surface: A gardener asks how the bloom in the herbaceous border smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick for a river, something that flows; this one forms much of the border between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: The river runs along the German-Polish frontier, so it is a frontier stream, a thing that flows.

clue.text: 15 has crop with wretched fancy tail

indicators.note: tail means come at the back, so the word for fancy follows the others

parts.note: a riding crop is a whip
poor means wretched or pitiable
will is wish or desire, what one fancies

explanation.surface: A rider with a crop has a miserable, ornate tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '15' refers to the answer at 15 across, a creature active after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American nightjar calls at dusk, so it is a bird of the night.

clue.text: Circus dancer shows familiarity with heroin

parts.note: taking a liberty means being overfamiliar, so familiarity can be a liberty
horse is old drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A circus performer gets too cosy and is found with hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancer' suggests a person, but this is a horse that performs riderless in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A riderless performing animal that goes through set steps in the ring is a kind of circus dancer.

clue.text: Bury bear and get cross

parts.note: to inter is to bury
to bear young is to breed

explanation.surface: Someone buries a bear and becomes angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get cross' reads as becoming angry but means produce crosses, hybrid offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals of different strains that mate produce hybrids, which is crossing them.

clue.text: Crop expert cooking mint or sago

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of mint or sago are mixed up like ingredients

explanation.surface: A specialist in plants is preparing mint or sago for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An agronomist studies soil and field-crop production.

clue.text: One who goes out late for a jar, perhaps?

definitions.text: One who goes out late for a jar, perhaps?

parts.words: One who goes out late for a jar, perhaps?
parts.note: reads as a drinker popping out after dark for a pint, but a jar is also short for a nightjar, a bird active after dusk

explanation.walkthrough: 'A jar' is British slang for a drink of beer; it also hints at the nightjar, a bird that hunts after dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps late hours, like an owl or nightjar, is called by this name for creatures of the dark.

clue.text: In game of chance, getting inside information is sheer necessity.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the game of chance is getting the information inside it, enclosing it

parts.note: dice is a game of chance
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: In a gamble, getting inside knowledge becomes a matter of pure need.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British slang for information, as in 'the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigence is extreme poverty, being in dire need or want.

clue.text: Trimmer has equal footing with a sovereign

parts.note: being on a par means being on an equal footing
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone who trims things stands level with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or person that pares, cutting off peel or edges, is a trimmer.

clue.text: Run away together, or hang about in quarters?

indicators.note: in places the word for hanging about between the two compass quarters

parts.note: east is one of the four quarters of the compass; two of them give E and E
to lop is to hang loosely or droop, as in lop-eared

explanation.surface: Lovers run off together, or perhaps they just loiter around their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' reads as lodgings but means points of the compass; two Easts surround the word for drooping.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who flee to marry secretly run off together.

clue.text: Embarrass dancing club member by sudden attack

parts.note: a disco is a club for dancing
M is a standard abbreviation for member, as in MP
a fit is a sudden attack of illness or temper

explanation.surface: A member of a dance club suffers a seizure and is mortified.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit someone is to make them uneasy or disconcerted.

clue.text: Having put note on returned volume, he issues tickets

definitions.text: Having put note on returned volume, he issues tickets

parts.words: Having put note on returned volume, he issues tickets
parts.note: describes the person who records each reservation in a ledger and sells tickets at the window

explanation.walkthrough: A loose cryptic definition of the old-style kind: noting a reservation is making a booking, and the official who does it at a station also sells the tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway or theatre official who records reservations and sells tickets has this job title.

clue.text: Physician can afford a sail

explanation.surface: A doctor is rich enough to buy a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition: a sail affords, that is has, a leech, the name for its trailing edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors were once called by the name of the bloodsucking worm they used, and that word also names the after edge of a fore-and-aft sail.

clue.text: We're told it's full agreement

indicators.note: we're told signals that a spoken word is heard and the entry is its sound-alike

parts.note: packed means full

explanation.surface: Rumour has it the agreement is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty.

clue.text: Count up what is a fair reward

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to deem is to judge or count, as in count yourself lucky

explanation.surface: Someone totals up what a just payment would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Meed is an old word for a deserved recompense or due.

clue.text: One move a player can make.

definitions.text: One move a player can make.

parts.words: One move a player can make.
parts.note: reads as a game move, but the player is an actor and the move is leaving the stage, a standard stage direction

explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests chess or a sport; here it is an actor, and the move is the stage direction for going off.
explanation.definitionFit: A script's direction for an actor leaving the stage is one movement a performer makes.

clue.text: Nice detail could be near the knuckle

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the two words might be made into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: A nice detail in a story might turn out to be rather risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Near the knuckle is a British idiom for close to being improper or offensive, which is what indecent or coarse means.

clue.text: Be weak because aged and hammer-toed

indicators.note: hammer here means beat out of shape, so the letters of toed are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is feeble because they are old and suffer from a deformed toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer-toed' reads as a foot condition; 'hammer' is the anagram signal and 'toed' the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in one's dotage is to have weakened mental powers through old age.

clue.text: Full of alcohol, married woman heard to make a date

indicators.note: heard tells us a woman's name is spoken and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: Ethel is a woman's name

indicators.note: to make a means the letters of date are formed into something different

explanation.surface: A married woman, it is said, arranges a romantic meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' turns the name ETHEL into ETHYL; 'to make a' rearranges DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit that has been methylated has methanol added to industrial alcohol, so it is laced with alcohol.
